recognize_zh: 抹片中只有一顆淡染、邊緣帶紫色顆粒狀沉積的單核細胞，細胞核輪廓不清；此圖單獨看無法確認毛狀細胞的毛狀突起，需配合標題與酸性磷酸酶（TRAP）或流式細胞儀判讀。
features: Single pale mononuclear cell roughly twice the size of adjacent red cells
Purple granular deposits concentrated at the cell periphery with sparse central granules
Nucleus poorly delineated; chromatin detail not assessable
No clearly defined circumferential hairy projections
Background red cells with slit-like central pallor (stomatocyte-like drying artifact)
describe_en: Smear shows a single pale mononuclear cell with purple granular deposits concentrated at the periphery of the cytoplasm and a poorly delineated nucleus. Distinct hairy cytoplasmic projections are not evident, and the staining pattern raises the possibility of a cytochemical preparation rather than a routine Romanowsky stain. The surrounding red cells show slit-like central pallor, likely artifactual. Morphology in this single field is not diagnostic on its own; correlation with TRAP cytochemistry and flow cytometry (CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123) is required to support hairy cell leukemia.

ddx.vs: A degenerated basophil retains coarse metachromatic granules and a lobulated nucleus, whereas hairy cells have a round-oval nucleus with pale agranular cytoplasm and TRAP positivity.
Monocytes have a folded nucleus, gray-blue vacuolated cytoplasm with fine granules and are nonspecific esterase positive, CD14 positive and CD103 negative.
Villous lymphocytes show short polar villi with basophilic cytoplasm and are TRAP weak/negative, CD103 and annexin A1 negative.
